Inhibition of SIRT1 impairs nuclear FoxO1 accumulation and MDR2 expression and augments the cytotoxic effects of paclitaxel and doxorubicin in tamoxifen-resistant cells. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of FoxO1- and MDR2-mediated chemoresistance. By driving drug-efflux capacity in resistant cells, SIRT1 reduces the efficacy of endocrine therapy and other agents.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 promotes cisplatin resistance in non-small-cell lung cancer cells by elevating expression of vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A). SIRT1 is upregulated in cisplatin-resistant tumor tissues and cells compared with cisplatin-sensitive groups, correlating with the resistant phenotype. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of VEGF-A-mediated chemoresistance. By enhancing VEGF-A, SIRT1 may support tumor survival and adaptive responses that blunt the cytotoxic effects of cisplatin. This identifies SIRT1 as a potential target for overcoming chemotherapy resistance in lung cancer, since inhibiting SIRT1 could lower VEGF-A and re-sensitize resistant tumors to platinum-based treatment.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 promotes DNA damage repair and radioresistance through the ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM)-Chk2 pathway in non-small-cell lung cancer cells. By supporting this DNA-damage-response branch, SIRT3 enables cancer cells to survive ionizing radiation more effectively. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of enhanced DNA repair and radiation resistance. This has therapeutic implications, because combining SIRT3 inhibition with radiotherapy could impair the repair of radiation-induced damage and thereby improve treatment efficacy.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 overexpression inhibits the generation of key glycolytic enzymes in A549 cells, suppressing glycolysis and thereby enhancing the sensitivity of these lung cancer cells to radiation. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of suppressed glycolytic metabolism and increased radiation sensitivity. Because glycolytic metabolism supports tumor survival and DNA repair under stress, curtailing it makes cells more vulnerable to radiation-induced damage. This suggests that SIRT6 activation, or strategies that mimic its metabolic effects, could improve the efficacy of radiotherapy in lung cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 upregulates expression of the cell-cycle inhibitor genes p16 and p21, while suppressing CyclinB1/Cdc2 and Cdc25c, and this cell-cycle blockade induces apoptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis induction. By enforcing these checkpoints, SIRT4 functions as a tumor suppressor in liver cancer, limiting proliferation and promoting death of transformed cells. The coordinated upregulation of p16 and p21 with suppression of cell-cycle drivers reflects SIRT4's broad influence on the machinery that governs entry into mitosis. This supports interest in SIRT4 as a therapeutic target for hepatocellular carcinoma.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 downregulates both the mRNA and protein levels of glutathione S-transferase pi 1 (GSTP1), a phase II detoxification enzyme involved in the metabolism of chemotherapeutic agents. SIRT3 overexpression promotes sorafenib-induced apoptosis and thereby enhances the drug sensitivity of hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of reduced GSTP1 and enhanced drug responsiveness. By lowering the capacity of cancer cells to detoxify sorafenib, SIRT3 restores sensitivity to this agent. This suggests that SIRT3 expression status could predict sorafenib response in liver cancer, and that boosting SIRT3 may help overcome drug resistance in this malignancy.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell growth through induction of apoptosis, inhibition of oxidative stress, and blockade of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of JAK2/STAT3 blockade and tumor suppression. By restraining this oncogenic signaling axis, SIRT6 limits the proliferative and survival signals that drive liver cancer progression. The combination of apoptosis induction and oxidative-stress suppression reflects SIRT6's multi-pronged tumor-suppressive activity. This positions SIRT6 as a promising target for hepatocellular carcinoma, where restoring or enhancing SIRT6 function could complement existing treatments.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 contributes to colorectal carcinogenesis by enhancing glutaminolysis in a deglutarylation-dependent manner, promoting cancer cell metabolism and proliferation. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of enhanced glutamine catabolism in colorectal cancer. By supporting the use of glutamine as a fuel and carbon source, SIRT5 provides tumor cells with the metabolic flexibility required for rapid growth. This oncogenic function illustrates that sirtuins can promote as well as suppress cancer, depending on the tissue and the specific metabolic demands of the tumor. Inhibiting SIRT5 may therefore be a strategy to starve colorectal cancer cells of the glutamine-dependent metabolism they rely on.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: Endothelial-cell-specific overexpression of SIRT1 protects against atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice, and this protection is associated with inhibition of endothelial cell apoptosis through activation of eNOS expression. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of eNOS-dependent vascular protection. By maintaining nitric oxide production and limiting endothelial cell death, SIRT1 preserves endothelial function and resists the progression of atherosclerotic lesions. This positions SIRT1 as an atheroprotective factor in the vasculature and supports efforts to activate SIRT1 as a strategy against cardiovascular disease.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 decreases atherosclerotic plaque formation in LDL receptor-deficient mice by regulating macrophage polarization. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of anti-atherogenic macrophage phenotypes. By steering macrophages toward less inflammatory states, SIRT2 reduces the foam-cell accumulation and chronic inflammation that drive plaque development. This links SIRT2 to innate immune modulation in vascular disease, complementing the anti-inflammatory actions of other sirtuins. Because macrophages are central to atherosclerosis, interventions that preserve SIRT2 activity in these cells could help limit plaque burden and stabilize existing lesions, reducing the risk of cardiovascular events.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 protects against endothelial dysfunction, vascular smooth muscle cell senescence, and atherosclerosis in mice through multiple mechanisms, including deacetylation of H3K9 at inflammatory gene promoters and suppression of NF-kappaB signaling. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of vascular homeostasis. By restraining inflammatory gene expression and maintaining endothelial and smooth muscle function, SIRT6 resists the cellular changes that drive atherogenesis. This places SIRT6 among the key sirtuins defending the vasculature against age-related dysfunction.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 protein levels are substantially decreased in the lungs of patients with COPD and emphysema, as well as in the lungs of rodents exposed to cigarette smoke. SIRT1 has anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and antioxidant roles in COPD pathogenesis. Directionally, COPD and smoke exposure sit upstream of reduced SIRT1. Because SIRT1 normally dampens inflammation and oxidative stress, its depletion contributes to the progressive tissue damage and airspace destruction seen in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT6
context: Reduced SIRT6 expression is associated with COPD development through enhancement of cellular senescence that arises from insufficient autophagy during cigarette smoke exposure. SIRT6 deficiency impairs autophagy and promotes premature senescence in lung cells. Directionally, SIRT6 deficiency sits upstream of impaired autophagy and accelerated cellular aging in the lung. By failing to clear damaged components, cells accumulate and enter senescence, contributing to the structural remodeling and functional decline characteristic of COPD.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 inhibits mitochondrial oxidative stress in airway epithelial cells, and this action contributes to attenuating the progression of COPD. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of reduced airway epithelial oxidative stress. By curbing mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, SIRT3 protects airway cells from the damage inflicted by cigarette smoke and chronic inflammation. Activating the SIRT3 signaling pathway is therefore proposed as a novel therapeutic strategy to slow or prevent COPD pathogenesis. This highlights mitochondrial sirtuins as potential drug targets in chronic lung disease, where oxidative stress is a central driver of tissue injury.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3 deficiency
context: SIRT3 deficiency in the aging murine lung promotes a fibrotic response mediated by TGF-beta1 and augments mitochondrial DNA damage and apoptosis in alveolar epithelial cells. Conversely, SIRT3 overexpression can ameliorate asbestos-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Directionally, SIRT3 deficiency sits upstream of enhanced TGF-beta1-driven fibrosis, because by weakening mitochondrial antioxidant defenses it renders alveolar epithelial cells vulnerable to the damage that fuels the fibrotic program. Restoring SIRT3 could therefore protect against pulmonary fibrosis, making mitochondrial sirtuin activity an important determinant of lung resilience to environmental and aging-related fibrotic injury.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 enhances allergic asthmatic inflammation by upregulating T-helper type 2 responses and macrophage polarization. Pharmacologic ablation of SIRT2 attenuates, while genetic SIRT2 overexpression exaggerates, the allergic asthmatic phenotype. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of Th2-driven allergic inflammation. By promoting the type 2 immune response characteristic of asthma, SIRT2 amplifies airway inflammation and the associated pathology. This makes SIRT2 inhibition a candidate therapeutic approach for allergic asthma, since reducing SIRT2 activity could dampen Th2 responses and macrophage-mediated inflammation, providing a potential strategy to modulate the severity of the disease.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT6
context: Upregulated SIRT6 ameliorates airway remodeling in asthma through regulation of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, representing a protective role against structural airway changes. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of suppressed EMT and preserved airway architecture. By restraining the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition that contributes to airway remodeling, SIRT6 helps maintain the normal structure of the airways during chronic inflammation. This protective function contrasts with the profibrotic role of SIRT7 in asthma and suggests that the balance of sirtuin activities shapes disease outcome.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT7
context: Upregulated SIRT7 promotes airway remodeling in asthma by regulating TGF-beta1-induced airway smooth muscle cell proliferation and migration, contrasting with SIRT6's protective role in the same disease. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of profibrotic airway changes. By supporting smooth muscle growth and movement in response to TGF-beta1, SIRT7 contributes to the thickening and architectural distortion of the airway wall that characterizes chronic asthma. This profibrotic function makes SIRT7 inhibition a potential therapeutic strategy to limit airway remodeling. The opposing actions of SIRT7 and SIRT6 in asthma illustrate the importance of sirtuin specificity in lung disease.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: Unbalanced p53/SIRT1 axis
context: The unbalanced p53/SIRT1 axis may impact lymphocyte homeostasis in COVID-19 patients. COVID-19 is characterized by increased p53 transcription in circulating lymphocytes and a persistently activated form of p53, possibly due to low SIRT1 levels. Directionally, low SIRT1 and elevated p53 activity sit upstream of disturbed lymphocyte homeostasis. Because SIRT1 normally deacetylates p53 and restrains its pro-apoptotic activity, its deficiency could leave lymphocytes vulnerable to p53-driven apoptosis and contribute to the lymphopenia seen in severe disease. Increased SIRT1 expression might therefore help alleviate COVID-19 pathogenesis by restoring the balance of this axis.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3 levels
context: Serum SIRT3 levels are markedly lower in severe COVID-19 patients compared with those with mild or moderate disease, indicating a positive role of SIRT3 in alleviating COVID-19. Directionally, SIRT3 levels sit upstream of clinical outcome and prognosis. Because SIRT3 supports mitochondrial antioxidant defense and dampens inflammation, its reduction in severe cases may permit greater oxidative stress and inflammatory damage. SIRT3 levels therefore serve as an indicator of disease severity and associate with prognosis.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 has dose-dependent effects on cardiac hypertrophy: low (2.5-fold) or moderate (7.5-fold) overexpression attenuates hypertrophy, whereas high (12.5-fold) overexpression increases it. Directionally, SIRT1 expression level determines whether the outcome is protective or detrimental. This biphasic behavior explains conflicting reports in the literature on SIRT1's cardiac effects, which differ depending on the degree of overexpression studied. The finding underscores that more SIRT1 is not always better, and that therapeutic approaches must consider dosing windows.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 interacts with and activates PPARalpha to prevent the metabolic switch from fatty acid oxidation to glycolysis that occurs in cardiac hypertrophy. By promoting fatty acid oxidation gene expression and inactivating NF-kappaB, SIRT1 preserves the adult heart's preferred fuel preference. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of PPARalpha-dependent metabolic preservation. Maintaining fatty acid oxidation prevents the maladaptive glycolytic shift that accompanies hypertrophic growth and heart failure.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 protects against cardiac hypertrophy by inducing expression of the antioxidant proteins SOD2 and catalase. The SIRT3-mediated reduction in reactive oxygen species inhibits AKT signaling and the downstream gene expression associated with hypertrophy induction. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of antioxidant defense and hypertrophy suppression, since by lowering mitochondrial oxidative stress it removes a key stimulus for the growth signaling that drives pathological cardiac enlargement. This places mitochondrial sirtuin activity at the center of the redox control governing cardiac stress responses.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 functions as a negative regulator of cardiac hypertrophy by co-repressing c-Jun-dependent transcription at the chromatin level, thereby inhibiting downstream IGF-AKT signaling. In vivo inhibition of IGF signaling in SIRT6 knockout mice abrogates the hypertrophic response. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of suppressed c-Jun transcription and IGF-AKT signaling. By restraining this growth-promoting axis, SIRT6 limits the pathological growth signals that drive cardiac hypertrophy. The observation that blocking IGF signaling rescues the hypertrophic phenotype confirms that this pathway mediates the effect.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: SIRT3 gene
context: The human SIRT3 gene is deleted in up to 20% of all human cancers analyzed overall, and in up to 40% of breast and ovarian cancers. This frequent deletion establishes SIRT3 as a tumor suppressor that acts through reactive oxygen species suppression and metabolic regulation. Directionally, SIRT3 loss sits upstream of increased tumorigenesis susceptibility. By removing mitochondrial antioxidant protection, deletion of SIRT3 raises oxidative stress that can drive oncogenic signaling and genomic damage. The high deletion frequency, especially in breast and ovarian cancer, suggests SIRT3 status is an important determinant of cancer risk and may have prognostic value.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: SIRT6 locus
context: A survey of approximately one thousand human cancer cell lines revealed that the SIRT6 locus was deleted in 35% of the samples. This high deletion frequency supports SIRT6's role as a tumor suppressor that acts through repression of HIF-1alpha and c-MYC and suppression of glycolytic metabolic reprogramming. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of enhanced oncogenic metabolism and tumor growth. Without SIRT6, the brakes on aerobic glycolysis and proliferation are released, promoting the metabolic phenotype that sustains cancer. The prevalence of SIRT6 deletion across diverse cancer cell lines underscores its broad importance in restraining malignancy.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 inhibits the transcriptional activities of c-MYC, resulting in repression of the glycolytic metabolic reprogramming that supports tumor growth. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of c-MYC inhibition and tumor suppression. This complements SIRT6's repression of HIF-1alpha, giving SIRT6 a dual brake on the two major oncogenic drivers of glycolysis. By restricting the metabolic switch to aerobic glycolysis, SIRT6 limits the biosynthetic and energetic advantages that cancer cells depend on. This positions SIRT6 as a central regulator of the metabolic reprogramming that underlies many cancers and as a rational target for therapeutic activation.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: SIRT6
context: In a mouse liver cancer model, increased SIRT6 expression reduces survivin expression by deacetylating H3K9Ac at the survivin promoter, and this induces apoptosis during cancer initiation. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of survivin suppression and prevention of tumor initiation. By silencing survivin, an anti-apoptotic factor, SIRT6 removes a key block to programmed cell death in early tumor cells. This allows damaged or transformed cells to undergo apoptosis rather than expand into tumors. The finding links SIRT6's epigenetic control of a critical survival gene to its tumor-suppressive activity in the liver.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: SIRT6
context: Ectopic SIRT6 overexpression results in increased p53- and p73-dependent apoptosis through the ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM) kinase, and this effect requires SIRT6's mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of ATM-dependent activation of p53 and p73. This reveals a deacetylation-independent tumor-suppressive mechanism of SIRT6, in which its enzymatic transfer of ADP-ribose rather than histone deacetylation triggers the cell-death program. By engaging the p53 family, SIRT6 can eliminate stressed or transformed cells before they become established tumors. This expands our understanding of sirtuin catalytic diversity in cancer suppression.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: CD38
context: CD38, the major NADase in many mouse tissues, increases with age and depletes cellular NAD+ pools, thereby compromising sirtuin function. Mice lacking CD38 show elevated NAD+ levels and increased SIRT1 activity, coupled with protection from diet-induced obesity. Directionally, age-related CD38 upregulation sits upstream of NAD+ depletion and reduced sirtuin activity. Because sirtuins depend on NAD+ as a co-substrate, the rising NAD+ consumption by CD38 during aging starves sirtuin enzymes of their fuel. This makes CD38 a key target for NAD+-restoring interventions, and CD38 inhibition is being explored as a way to preserve NAD+ and support sirtuin function during aging.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan.md

subject: PARP1 and PARP2
context: PARP1 and PARP2 are major NAD+-consuming enzymes whose activity can deplete cellular NAD+ pools and compromise sirtuin function, creating competition for the same limited co-substrate. Directionally, PARP activity sits upstream of NAD+ consumption and reduced sirtuin availability. This competition is especially relevant during DNA damage, when PARP activation surges and rapidly consumes NAD+ to synthesize ADP-ribose polymers. Because both PARPs and sirtuins are essential for genome maintenance and stress responses, their shared dependence on NAD+ creates an intrinsic trade-off.
source_document: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md

subject: SARM1
context: SARM1 is an NAD+-consuming enzyme that, along with PARP1, PARP2, and CD38, can deplete cellular NAD+ pools and compromise sirtuin function. Directionally, SARM1 activity sits upstream of NAD+ depletion and impaired sirtuin signaling. Its activity is particularly relevant in neuronal contexts, where NAD+ depletion drives axonal degeneration. By consuming NAD+ upon injury or stress, SARM1 can starve sirtuins of their co-substrate at the very moment when their protective functions are most needed. This makes SARM1 an attractive therapeutic target for neurodegenerative conditions, where preventing NAD+ loss could preserve both axonal integrity and sirtuin activity.
source_document: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 deacetylates PGC-1alpha and amplifies expression of the circadian transcription factors BMAL1 and CLOCK. A key target of the BMAL1-CLOCK complex is NAMPT, establishing a circadian NAD+ biosynthesis cycle that rhythmically activates and deactivates SIRT1 in alignment with the daily cycle. Directionally, the NAMPT-NAD+ cycle sits upstream of rhythmic SIRT1 activity. Because SIRT1 feeds back to regulate clock components, this forms a stable oscillator coupling metabolism to circadian time. Disruption of this loop, as seen with aging and shift work, impairs both circadian function and metabolic health.
source_document: _document_ - SIRT1 Protein roles at the nexus of health, disease, and therapeutics.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 can coordinate with the chromatin remodeler chromodomain-helicase-DNA-binding 4 (CHD4) to promote chromatin relaxation and DNA repair, exerting an anticarcinogenic role in lung cancer. Directionally, SIRT6 and CHD4 cooperation sits upstream of enhanced DNA repair capacity. By opening chromatin at sites of damage, the pair facilitates access of repair machinery and promotes accurate repair of DNA lesions. This reduces the genomic instability that drives cancer initiation and progression. The finding highlights how sirtuins partner with chromatin remodelers to maintain genome integrity, and it supports SIRT6 as a relevant target in lung cancer prevention and therapy.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT6 silencing
context: SIRT6 silencing can overcome sorafenib resistance by promoting ferroptosis in gastric cancer, suggesting a therapeutic strategy for resistant malignancies. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of ferroptotic cell death and restored drug sensitivity. By triggering this iron-dependent form of cell death, SIRT6 depletion bypasses the resistance mechanisms that allow gastric cancer cells to survive sorafenib treatment. This reveals an unexpected pro-survival role for SIRT6 in this context, where its activity protects cells from ferroptosis.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 overexpression dramatically suppresses the metastatic capability of ovarian cancer cells by inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through downregulation of Twist, a key EMT transcription factor. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of Twist suppression and maintenance of an epithelial phenotype. By reducing Twist, SIRT3 blocks the switch that confers migratory and invasive behavior on tumor cells. This restrains the metastatic spread that is the main cause of ovarian cancer mortality. The finding positions SIRT3 as a suppressor of ovarian cancer metastasis and suggests that maintaining SIRT3 activity could help limit disease dissemination.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 promotes cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer by suppressing DNA damage in a ROS-dependent manner through regulation of the Nrf2/Heme Oxygenase-1 pathway. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of Nrf2-mediated chemoresistance. By activating this antioxidant program, SIRT5 helps cancer cells neutralize the reactive oxygen species that contribute to cisplatin-induced DNA damage. This reduces the genotoxic burden of the drug and blunts its cytotoxicity, allowing tumor cells to survive treatment. Inhibiting SIRT5, therefore, could re-sensitize ovarian cancer cells to cisplatin by dismantling their antioxidant defenses.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1-mediated PAK1 deacetylation at K420
context: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1) at lysine 420 hinders autophagy and glioblastoma growth, establishing SIRT1 as a tumor suppressor in this context. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic inhibition of PAK1 sits upstream of suppressed glioblastoma progression. By restraining PAK1 activity, SIRT1 limits the autophagy that glioblastoma cells rely on to survive under metabolic stress. This impairs tumor growth and positions SIRT1 as a brake on an aggressive brain malignancy. The finding illustrates that the same sirtuin can exert opposite effects in different cancers, and it suggests SIRT1 activation as a therapeutic direction for glioblastoma.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 stabilizes the interaction between Ku70 and Bax to enhance the viability of glioma cells, representing an oncogenic function in this cancer type that contrasts with its tumor-suppressive roles elsewhere. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of enhanced glioma cell survival. By keeping Bax sequestered by Ku70, SIRT3 prevents the pro-apoptotic protein from triggering mitochondrial cell death, allowing glioma cells to evade apoptosis. This oncogenic facet complicates the picture of SIRT3 as a universal tumor suppressor and underscores that its net effect depends on cellular context. In gliomas, SIRT3 inhibition might be a strategy to promote tumor cell death.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 affects the malignancy of glioma cells mainly by promoting glioma proliferation and invasion through the ERK and STAT3 signaling pathways. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of ERK- and STAT3-driven glioma progression. By sustaining these proliferative and invasive signaling cascades, SIRT7 supports the aggressive growth and spread characteristic of glioma. This identifies SIRT7 as a pro-tumorigenic factor in this brain cancer and suggests that SIRT7 inhibition could suppress glioma progression. The finding adds to the emerging picture of SIRT7 as an oncogenic sirtuin in certain malignancies, where its functions diverge from the longevity-promoting roles of other family members.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 promotes the progression of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia by regulating the phosphorylation and degradation of the cell-cycle inhibitor p27 through deacetylation of cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2). Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of CDK2-dependent cell-cycle progression in leukemia. By licensing CDK2 activity, SIRT1 promotes the degradation of p27 and thereby removes a brake on cell-cycle entry, fueling leukemic proliferation. This makes SIRT1 a promoter of T-ALL progression and identifies SIRT1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy to restore p27-mediated cell-cycle control and suppress leukemic growth.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT2 inhibition
context: Inhibition of SIRT2 suppresses the in vitro growth and in vivo engraftment of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells through diminished deacetylation of LIM domain only 2 (LMO2). Directionally, SIRT2 inhibition sits upstream of LMO2-dependent leukemia suppression. LMO2 is a key oncogenic transcription factor in T-ALL, and its activity depends on deacetylation by SIRT2. Blocking SIRT2 reduces LMO2 function, impairing both the expansion of leukemic cells in culture and their ability to engraft in vivo. This identifies SIRT2 inhibition as a promising approach for T-ALL therapy, targeting a central oncogenic driver in this disease.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: Overall SIRT1 knockout mice are highly susceptible to sepsis-induced inflammatory lung injury due to activation of the proinflammatory transcription factor NF-kappaB. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of heightened inflammatory lung damage. Because SIRT1 normally deacetylates and restrains NF-kappaB, its absence removes a key brake on inflammatory gene expression during sepsis. This unleashes an exaggerated inflammatory response that damages the lung, illustrating SIRT1's protective role in acute inflammatory injury. Restoring SIRT1 activity may therefore help dampen the excessive inflammation that complicates sepsis and contributes to acute respiratory failure.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 promotes the expression of manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD), and this regulation is crucial for the protective effect of SIRT3 on hyperoxia-induced acute lung injury. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of MnSOD-dependent lung protection. By maintaining MnSOD, SIRT3 supports mitochondrial antioxidant defense against the oxidative stress generated by high oxygen exposure. This shields lung tissue from the reactive oxygen species that drive injury during hyperoxia. The finding highlights SIRT3 as a mitochondrial antioxidant guardian in the lung and suggests that strategies to enhance SIRT3 or MnSOD could protect against oxygen-induced lung damage in clinical settings.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 regulates macrophage polarization to alleviate sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome via dual mechanisms that are both dependent on and independent of autophagy. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotypes in lung injury. By steering macrophages away from proinflammatory states, SIRT6 dampens the excessive inflammatory response that drives ARDS, while its autophagy-related actions support cellular quality control. This coordinated regulation helps limit lung damage during sepsis.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SNHG10
context: The long noncoding RNA SNHG10 upregulates the tumor-suppressive sirtuin SIRT1 in non-small-cell lung cancer by sponging miR-543, relieving microRNA-mediated repression of SIRT1 expression. Directionally, SNHG10 acts upstream of SIRT1 abundance in the NSCLC ceRNA network. By sequestering miR-543, SNHG10 raises SIRT1 levels, and this upregulation underlies the lncRNA's tumor-suppressive activity in lung cancer. The finding highlights how noncoding RNAs can tune sirtuin expression and thereby influence the balance between tumor suppression and tumor promotion in specific cancer contexts.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1, when upregulated by the long noncoding RNA SNHG10, suppresses proliferation of non-small-cell lung cancer cells, acting as a tumor suppressor in this context. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of restrained NSCLC growth. This tumor-suppressive role of SIRT1 in lung cancer contrasts with the oncogenic functions SIRT1 displays in other settings, underscoring the strong context dependence of sirtuin biology. The finding implicates SIRT1 as a mediator of SNHG10's anti-proliferative effects and suggests that sustaining SIRT1 expression may limit NSCLC cell expansion.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: circ_0001946
context: The circular RNA circ_0001946 upregulates SIRT1, and the resulting SIRT1 activity promotes cell growth in lung adenocarcinoma by activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Directionally, circ_0001946 sits upstream of SIRT1 upregulation, which in turn drives oncogenic Wnt signaling. This represents a tumor-promoting axis in lung adenocarcinoma that is opposite to the tumor-suppressive SIRT1 effect mediated by SNHG10 in NSCLC, illustrating how different noncoding RNAs can direct SIRT1 toward opposing outcomes in the same tissue.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1, upregulated by circ_0001946, promotes cell growth in lung adenocarcinoma by activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of β-catenin-driven proliferation in this lung cancer subtype. This oncogenic SIRT1 function contrasts with the tumor-suppressive anti-proliferative effect SIRT1 exerts in non-small-cell lung cancer when induced by SNHG10, demonstrating that SIRT1's role in lung cancer depends on the tumor subtype and the signaling context.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
object: osteopontin-induced NF-κB p65 acetylation and EMT
context: Overexpression of SIRT1 protects non-small-cell lung cancer cells against osteopontin-induced NF-κB p65 acetylation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, thereby attenuating osteopontin-driven cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of dampened NF-κB signaling and EMT in response to the pro-metastatic cytokine osteopontin. By deacetylating p65 and restraining EMT, SIRT1 limits the invasive and proliferative program that osteopontin triggers in NSCLC cells, supporting a tumor-suppressive role in this context.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 deacetylates the K100 residue of the glycolytic enzyme phosphoglycerate mutase and facilitates its activation, which results in enhanced NADPH production and accelerated tumor growth in non-small-cell lung cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatic modification of phosphoglycerate mutase sits upstream of increased glycolytic flux and anabolic support for tumor growth. This oncogenic action of SIRT2 in lung cancer contrasts with its tumor-suppressive deacetylation of AKR1C1 in the same disease, illustrating the context dependence of SIRT2's cancer-related functions.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1 silencing
context: Silencing of SIRT1 enhances the cisplatin sensitivity of H1299/cisplatin non-small-cell lung cancer cells by suppressing autophagy. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of reduced autophagic survival signaling and increased susceptibility to cisplatin. Because autophagy can protect cancer cells from chemotherapy-induced damage, its suppression re-sensitizes resistant NSCLC cells to cisplatin. This identifies SIRT1 inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome platinum resistance in lung cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT2 upregulation
context: Upregulation of SIRT2 in non-small-cell lung cancer cells increases their sensitivity to cisplatin treatment, while the opposite modulation reduces responsiveness. Directionally, SIRT2 levels sit upstream of platinum chemosensitivity in NSCLC. Higher SIRT2 expression renders tumor cells more vulnerable to cisplatin-induced killing, suggesting that SIRT2 activity could be exploited to improve the efficacy of platinum-based therapy in lung cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 reduces cisplatin resistance in lung cancer by modulating the FoxO3/Cdc10-dependent transcript 1 protein axis. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of restored platinum sensitivity in drug-resistant lung cancer cells. By acting through the FoxO3/CDT1 pathway, SIRT3 counteracts the survival adaptations that underlie cisplatin resistance, making SIRT3 activation a candidate strategy to re-sensitize resistant lung tumors to platinum-based chemotherapy.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: Serum SIRT3
object: lung cancer patients from healthy individuals
context: Serum SIRT3 distinguishes lung cancer patients from healthy individuals with an area under the curve of 0.918, an optimal cutoff value of 3.12, a sensitivity of 86.4%, and a specificity of 94%. Directionally, serum SIRT3 levels serve as a diagnostic biomarker for lung cancer. The high accuracy of SIRT3 in discriminating cancer patients supports its use as a blood-based marker for lung cancer screening or early detection, complementing SIRT expression differences observed between tumor and non-tumor lung tissue.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 prevents tumor immune evasion and suppresses the development of hepatocellular carcinoma by orchestrating bile acid metabolism. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of anti-tumor immunity and restrained HCC growth. By shaping the bile acid milieu, SIRT5 influences the immune microenvironment of the liver tumor, reducing the ability of HCC to evade immune destruction. This tumor-suppressive metabolic function contrasts with SIRT5's glycolysis-reprogramming role that can promote HCC growth, reflecting SIRT5's context-dependent effects in liver cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT5
object: HCC growth and metastasis via glycolysis reprogramming
context: Activation of mitochondrial SIRT5 promotes the growth and metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma cells via glucose metabolism reprogramming from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of the glycolytic switch that fuels liver cancer progression. By favoring glycolysis, SIRT5 supplies the biosynthetic and bioenergetic demands of rapidly growing HCC cells, supporting tumor aggressiveness. This oncogenic role is opposed by SIRT5's bile-acid-metabolism-mediated suppression of HCC, underscoring the dual, context-dependent functions of SIRT5 in liver cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1 and SIRT6
object: hnRNP A1 to suppress glycolysis and growth in HCC
context: SIRT1 and SIRT6 deacetylate the RNA-binding protein hnRNP A1 to suppress glycolysis and growth in hepatocellular carcinoma. Directionally, SIRT1 and SIRT6 sit upstream of hnRNP A1 deacetylation, which curtails glycolytic gene expression and tumor growth. By restraining the glycolytic program through hnRNP A1, these nuclear sirtuins act as metabolic tumor suppressors in HCC, opposing the aerobic glycolysis that supports cancer cell proliferation.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6, stabilized by the deubiquitinase USP48, attenuates glycolysis in hepatocellular carcinoma and impedes metabolic reprogramming, thereby hampering HCC malignancy. Directionally, USP48-dependent stabilization of SIRT6 sits upstream of suppressed glycolytic metabolism and reduced tumor aggressiveness. By maintaining SIRT6 protein levels, USP48 sustains SIRT6-mediated repression of glycolysis, preventing the metabolic shift that fuels liver cancer growth. This identifies the USP48-SIRT6 axis as a potential therapeutic node in HCC.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
object: colorectal cancer via glutamine metabolism and apoptosis
context: SIRT1 affects colorectal cancer in a dose-dependent manner by regulating glutamine metabolism and apoptotic pathways. Heterozygous deletion of SIRT1 induces c-Myc expression, enhancing glutamine metabolism, proliferation, autophagy, and cancer formation, whereas homozygous deletion triggers apoptosis, increases cell death, diminishes autophagy, and reduces cancer formation. Directionally, SIRT1 expression level sits upstream of opposing metabolic and survival outcomes in CRC, explaining the dual roles of SIRT1 in colorectal tumorigenesis.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3
context: Overexpression of SIRT3 improves the resistance of colorectal cancer cells to anticancer drugs through regulation of superoxide dismutase 2 and PGC-1α. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of SOD2- and PGC-1α-dependent protective responses in CRC. By enhancing antioxidant and mitochondrial programs, SIRT3 reduces the vulnerability of CRC cells to chemotherapeutic agents, contributing to drug resistance. This resistance-promoting role should be weighed when considering SIRT3-targeted cancer therapy.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 increases the sensitivity of colorectal cancer cells to the chemotherapeutic drug 5-fluorouracil by inhibiting the cell cycle. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of cell-cycle arrest, which primes CRC cells for 5-fluorouracil-induced killing. By restraining proliferation, SIRT4 enhances the cytotoxic effect of the drug, suggesting that SIRT4 expression status could predict or improve responses to 5-fluorouracil-based therapy in colorectal cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1 upregulation
context: FoxQ1-mediated SIRT1 upregulation augments the expression and nuclear translocation of β-catenin and benefits CRC-related intestinal pathological bacteria, thereby enhancing the radioresistance of colorectal cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT1 upregulation sits upstream of β-catenin-driven survival and radiation resistance in CRC. By promoting β-catenin signaling, SIRT1 helps colorectal cancer cells survive ionizing radiation, which has implications for combining SIRT1 inhibition with radiotherapy to improve treatment outcomes.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1 depletion
context: SIRT1 depletion promotes gastric cancer progression through activation of the STAT3/MMP-13 signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of STAT3- and MMP-13-driven tumor progression in gastric cancer. Because SIRT1 normally restrains this pathway, its depletion unleashes STAT3 activation and MMP-13 expression, accelerating GC growth and invasion. This positions SIRT1 as a tumor suppressor in gastric cancer and identifies STAT3/MMP-13 signaling as a downstream mediator of SIRT1's protective effect.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT2
context: Overexpression of SIRT2 significantly enhances the sensitivity of cisplatin-resistant counterpart ovarian cancer cells to cisplatin. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of restored platinum sensitivity in resistant ovarian cancer cells. By increasing the vulnerability of these cells to cisplatin, SIRT2 may help overcome platinum resistance, a major obstacle in ovarian cancer treatment. This suggests that strategies to augment SIRT2 activity could improve the efficacy of cisplatin-based therapy in resistant disease.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 expression suppresses the expression and acetylation of high-mobility group box 1 protein, thereby inhibiting migration, invasion, and angiogenesis of ovarian cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of reduced HMGB1-driven metastatic and angiogenic programs. By dampening HMGB1, SIRT1 limits the invasive and blood-supply-supporting behaviors of ovarian cancer cells, supporting a tumor-suppressive role and identifying the SIRT1-HMGB1 axis as a candidate therapeutic target in ovarian cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
object: endometrial cancer growth and cisplatin resistance
context: SIRT1 promotes the growth and cisplatin resistance of endometrial cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of increased tumor-cell survival and reduced sensitivity to cisplatin in endometrial cancer. By supporting proliferative and survival programs, SIRT1 enables endometrial cancer cells to grow and to withstand platinum-based chemotherapy. This identifies SIRT1 as a potential therapeutic target for improving endometrial cancer treatment outcomes.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT2
object: endometrial cancer stemness and chemoresistance via MEK/ERK
context: SIRT2 promotes cell stemness and activates the MEK/ERK signaling pathway while repressing chemosensitivity in endometrial cancer. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of stem-like phenotypes and MEK/ERK-dependent survival in endometrial cancer cells. By enhancing stemness and ERK signaling, SIRT2 supports tumor self-renewal and reduces responsiveness to chemotherapy. This makes SIRT2 inhibition a potential strategy to sensitize endometrial cancer to treatment.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1 inhibition
object: glioma sensitivity to temozolomide via ROS
context: SIRT1 inhibition increases the sensitivity of glioma cells to temozolomide through facilitation of intracellular reactive oxygen species generation. Directionally, SIRT1 inhibition sits upstream of elevated ROS and enhanced drug-induced cell death in glioma. By blocking SIRT1's protective anti-oxidant activity, glioma cells accumulate ROS that sensitize them to temozolomide, the standard chemotherapy for glioblastoma. Combining SIRT1 inhibition with temozolomide may therefore improve treatment efficacy in malignant glioma.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3 overexpression
object: tamoxifen sensitivity in MTR-3 breast cancer cells
context: SIRT3 overexpression in the breast cancer cell line MTR-3 reduces the sensitivity of the resistant cells to tamoxifen. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of diminished responsiveness to endocrine therapy in breast cancer cells. By lowering tamoxifen sensitivity, SIRT3 may contribute to anti-estrogen resistance, complicating endocrine treatment of breast cancer. This is counterbalanced by SIRT4, which enhances tamoxifen sensitivity, highlighting opposing sirtuin functions in endocrine-resistant breast cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 enhances the tamoxifen sensitivity of breast cancer cells by inhibiting the STAT3 signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of restored endocrine responsiveness in breast cancer. By suppressing STAT3 signaling, SIRT4 makes breast cancer cells more vulnerable to tamoxifen, in contrast to SIRT3 overexpression, which reduces tamoxifen sensitivity. This positions SIRT4 as a potential enhancer of anti-estrogen therapy efficacy in breast cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: AMPK activation
object: SIRT1 activity in triple-negative breast cancer
context: AMPK activation reduces the expression of the oncogenic protein metadherin through enhanced SIRT1 activity, acting independently of GSK-3β in triple-negative breast cancer. Directionally, AMPK activation sits upstream of SIRT1-driven repression of metadherin. Because metadherin promotes cancer progression, metastasis, and chemoresistance, its downregulation via the AMPK-SIRT1 axis represents a tumor-suppressive mechanism in triple-negative breast cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT7 depletion
context: SIRT7 depletion inhibits tumor growth by activating p38/MAPK signaling in breast cancer. Directionally, SIRT7 loss sits upstream of p38/MAPK pathway activation, which suppresses tumor-cell expansion. Because SIRT7 normally restrains this growth-limiting signaling, its depletion unleashes p38/MAPK activity and curbs tumor growth. This positions SIRT7 as a tumor-promoting factor in breast cancer and identifies the p38/MAPK pathway as a downstream mediator.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1 knockdown
context: Pharmacological targeting or RNAi-mediated knockdown of SIRT1 inhibits cell growth and sensitizes acute myeloid leukemia cells to tyrosine kinase inhibitor treatment. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of enhanced drug sensitivity in AML. By restraining SIRT1-driven survival, AML cells become more responsive to tyrosine kinase inhibitors, suggesting that combining SIRT1 inhibition with TKI therapy could improve leukemia treatment outcomes.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: shSIRT6-induced DNA repair deficiency
context: SIRT6 knockdown-induced DNA repair deficiencies are potently synergistic with NAMPT targeting in acute myeloid leukemia treatment, showing promising in vivo efficacy compared with monotherapy. Directionally, SIRT6 loss-driven DNA repair defects and NAMPT inhibition cooperate to kill AML cells. This dual strategy exploits two vulnerabilities, offering a rationale for combination-based treatments that outperform single-agent therapy in acute myeloid leukemia.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 enables HPV-infected cervical cancer cells to continue growing by nullifying absent in melanoma 2 inflammasome-mediated immunity. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of suppressed inflammasome signaling and immune clearance in cervical cancer. By inactivating the AIM2 inflammasome, SIRT1 helps HPV-infected cervical cancer cells evade innate immune surveillance, supporting their continued growth. This positions the SIRT1-AIM2 axis as a potential immunotherapeutic target in HPV-driven cervical cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 contributes to the reprogramming of fatty acid synthesis by upregulating acetyl-coA carboxylase 1 to promote de novo lipogenesis through SIRT3 deacetylation, thereby promoting the invasion and metastasis of cervical cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of ACC1-driven de novo lipogenesis and metastatic behavior in cervical cancer. By enhancing lipid synthesis, SIRT3 supports the invasive and metastatic capabilities of cervical cancer cells, identifying SIRT3-ACC1 lipogenesis as a potential therapeutic target.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: MHY2245
context: MHY2245, a new SIRT1 inhibitor, exerts antitumor activity against ovarian cancer cells by blocking the pyruvate kinase M2/mTOR pathway. Directionally, MHY2245 sits upstream of suppressed PKM2/mTOR signaling and reduced ovarian cancer cell survival. By inhibiting SIRT1 and consequently the PKM2/mTOR pathway, MHY2245 curbs tumor-cell metabolism and growth. This supports SIRT1 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy in ovarian cancer, where SIRT1 inhibition of HMGB1 also suppresses metastasis and angiogenesis.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT5 loss
context: SIRT5 expression is directly correlated with favorable prognosis in pancreatic cancer, as SIRT5 loss promotes glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase 1 acetylation, thus promoting cell proliferation by enhancing glutamine and glutathione metabolism. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of GOT1 deacetylation that restrains pancreatic cancer growth. When SIRT5 is lost, GOT1 acetylation rises, boosting glutamine and glutathione metabolism to drive proliferation. This identifies SIRT5 as a tumor suppressor in pancreatic cancer whose levels could inform prognosis.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT6 upregulation
context: Upregulation of SIRT6 by the tumor suppressor KLF10 activity influences glycolysis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and distant metastasis of pancreatic cancer cells. Directionally, KLF10-driven SIRT6 upregulation sits upstream of altered metabolic and invasive behaviors in pancreatic cancer. By modulating glycolysis and EMT, SIRT6 shapes the aggressiveness and metastatic capacity of pancreatic cancer cells, indicating that the KLF10-SIRT6 axis may serve as a therapeutic or prognostic target in pancreatic cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 can facilitate chemoresistance of pancreatic cancer cells by regulating their adaptive response to chemotherapy-induced stress. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of stress adaptation and reduced drug sensitivity in pancreatic cancer. By helping tumor cells adapt to chemotherapy-induced stress, SIRT1 enables pancreatic cancer cells to survive cytotoxic treatment. This identifies SIRT1 as a potential target to overcome chemoresistance in pancreatic cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 can promote cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer by suppressing DNA damage in a ROS-dependent manner via regulation of the Nrf2/Heme Oxygenase-1 pathway. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of reduced ROS, diminished DNA damage, and enhanced survival of ovarian cancer cells treated with cisplatin. By activating Nrf2/HO-1-dependent antioxidant defense, SIRT5 protects ovarian cancer cells from platinum-induced damage, contributing to chemoresistance. This contrasts with SIRT2, whose overexpression enhances cisplatin sensitivity in resistant ovarian cancer cells.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

subject: Sirtuin deacetylation reaction
context: Sirtuin-catalyzed deacetylation couples the cleavage of NAD+ to the removal of acetyl groups from lysine residues. Each round of deacetylation converts one molecule of NAD+ into nicotinamide (NAM) and O-acetyl-ADP-ribose. NAM then acts as an end-product inhibitor of sirtuins by binding to a conserved pocket adjacent to the NAD+ site, thereby blocking further NAD+ hydrolysis. This product-based feedback links cellular NAD+ status and NAM levels directly to sirtuin enzymatic output.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: NAM (nicotinamide)
context: Nicotinamide is a known potent inhibitor of several classes of ribosylase enzymes that require NAD for their activity, as well as of SIRT1, the class III NAD+-dependent histone deacetylase. NAM acts as an end-product noncompetitive inhibitor of SIRT1 by binding to a conserved pocket adjacent to NAD+, thereby blocking NAD+ hydrolysis. Because NAM is generated by the sirtuin reaction itself, it provides a built-in negative feedback mechanism that can curtail SIRT1 activity when local nicotinamide accumulates.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: Sirtuins
context: The sirtuin family has been classified into five distinct classes (I-IV and U) based on a phylogenetic study of sirtuins from a wide range of prokaryotes and eukaryotes. SIR-2.1, Drosophila melanogaster Sir2 (D.mel1), Hst1, and SIRT1 all belong to subclass Ia. Subclass Ib includes Hst2, D.mel2, and various fungi and protozoa sirtuins along with SIRT2 and SIRT3. SIRT4 and SIRT5 belong to classes II and III, respectively. SIRT6 and SIRT7 belong to Class IV, which includes only eukaryotic sirtuins. Sir2 homologues from bacteria with undifferentiated motifs constitute class U.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: CobB
context: The first bacterial sirtuin was found in Salmonella enterica and was named CobB due to its involvement in cobalamin biosynthesis and propionic catabolism. CobB demonstrates that sirtuins are not restricted to eukaryotes but are also present in prokaryotes, where they regulate various metabolic pathways. In bacteria one or two sirtuins are typically found, and CobB serves as the founding example of prokaryotic sirtuin biology.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 activation enhances homologous recombination, a function that could help to decrease tumours by stabilising chromosomes and/or extending the lifespan by maintaining rDNA arrays. In human cells SIRT1 activation enhances homologous recombination. SIRT1 also contributes to telomere maintenance and augments global homologous recombination, linking nuclear sirtuin activity to genome stability and longevity.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 modulates the activity of DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1) by deacetylating it. Deacetylation of DNMT1 at certain lysine residues improves its methyltransferase activity, alters its transcription suppression activity, and impairs its ability to silence tumour suppressor genes. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of DNMT1 enzymatic activity and thus influences DNA methylation patterns and gene silencing, providing a direct molecular link between sirtuins and the epigenetic machinery.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 controls UV-induced DNA damage repair by deacetylating xeroderma pigmentosum group A (XPA), a protein that is required for the nucleotide excision repair pathway to function properly. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of XPA activity and thereby of nucleotide excision repair. This places SIRT1 in the DNA damage response network and links sirtuin function to the maintenance of genomic integrity following environmental genotoxic stress.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT1
object: oxidative stress and age-related NAD+ decline
context: SIRT1 has a significant role in oxidative stress response. Increased SIRT1 protein levels counteract oxidative stress and the ageing-related decline in NAD+ levels. In elderly humans SIRT1 protein expression shows a remarkable age-related increase against oxidative stress. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of cellular defence against oxidative damage, and its induction appears to be a compensatory anti-ageing response that mitigates the consequences of declining NAD+ availability.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT1 downregulation
context: Downregulation of SIRT1 was found to be important in the senescence of different types of endothelial cells. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of cellular senescence in the vascular endothelium. Because SIRT1 normally promotes stress resistance and genomic stability, its decline in endothelial cells is linked to the senescent phenotype. This positions SIRT1 as a potential target for preserving endothelial function and preventing vascular ageing.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT2
context: By targeting glycolytic enzymes, SIRT2 controls metabolic reprogramming during induced pluripotency. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of the metabolic switch from oxidative to glycolytic metabolism that accompanies reprogramming of somatic cells toward pluripotency. This metabolic control is essential for the establishment and function of primed human pluripotent stem cells, linking sirtuin activity to cell fate determination and stem cell biology.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 regulates HIF-1 activity, which is important for tumour hypoxia responses. HIF-1 protein stability and transcriptional activity are both negatively influenced by SIRT2, with SIRT2-mediated deacetylation necessary for HIF-1α destabilisation and the tumour cell hypoxia response. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of reduced HIF-1α abundance and activity, thereby restraining hypoxia-driven transcriptional programs in tumour cells.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT2
object: NSCLC cell lines and metastatic melanoma
context: The level of SIRT2 is upregulated in non-small cell lung cancer cell lines and in metastatic human melanoma tissues compared to healthy cells and tissues. Directionally, SIRT2 expression is increased in these aggressive cancer contexts. In metastatic melanoma, SIRT2 levels are increased compared to tumours of early stage, suggesting involvement of SIRT2 in the advancement of metastatic disease. SIRT2 therefore represents a potential biomarker and drug target in NSCLC and metastatic melanoma.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 could be a promising drug target for acute promyelocytic leukaemia therapy. Directionally, SIRT2 activity sits upstream of leukaemia cell survival and differentiation programs. Pharmacological modulation of SIRT2 is therefore being explored as a therapeutic strategy in this haematological malignancy, potentially by restoring differentiation or promoting death of leukaemic blasts.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 has a role in neurodegeneration and protects neural cells from oxidative damage caused by ageing and disease. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of neuronal resilience against oxidative stress. Although SIRT2 is overexpressed in neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's disease, its ability to shield neurons from oxidative injury suggests a protective function in specific contexts, and SIRT2 remains a candidate target for neuroprotective strategies.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT3
object: N-terminal 101 residues by mitochondrial processing peptidase
context: The full-length SIRT3 protein is enzymatically inactive and contains a mitochondrial targeting domain at its N-terminus. Mitochondrial matrix processing peptidase cleaves the N-terminal 101 residues, which then activates the enzyme. Directionally, proteolytic processing sits upstream of SIRT3 catalytic activity within the mitochondrial matrix. This maturation step ensures that SIRT3 functions only after import into mitochondria, where it deacetylates metabolic enzymes.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT3 deacetylase activity
context: The deacetylase activity of SIRT3 is required for viral suppression, and during infection SIRT3 keeps membrane potential and mitochondrial pH stable. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of mitochondrial homeostasis during viral infection, supporting antiviral defence. By maintaining mitochondrial function under infection-induced stress, SIRT3 protects cells from viral damage and restricts viral replication.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT3
context: Through the p53 pathway, SIRT3 prevents dysfunction and senescence caused by high glucose levels in endothelial cells by partially abrogating p53 activity. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of dampened p53 signalling and thereby of protection against glucose-induced endothelial senescence. This links mitochondrial sirtuin activity to vascular health and identifies SIRT3 as a potential target for preventing diabetic endothelial dysfunction.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 could also be used as a marker for colon cancer. In colon cancer, SIRT3 deficiency reduces cell proliferation, invasion, and migration while increasing apoptosis. Directionally, SIRT3 expression levels sit upstream of colon cancer behaviour, with loss of SIRT3 restraining tumour aggressiveness. SIRT3 therefore has potential diagnostic and prognostic utility in colorectal cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 stops mitochondrial reactive oxygen species generation, which inhibits HIF-1α and tumour growth. When SIRT3 is overexpressed, it resists the growth of established cancer cell lines. SIRT3 also prevents cancer cell metabolic reprogramming by destabilising HIF1α. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of reduced mitochondrial ROS and HIF-1α stabilisation, thereby opposing the hypoxic and metabolic adaptations that support tumour growth.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT3 activation
context: SIRT3 activation prevents amyotrophic lateral sclerosis motor neurons from developing metabolic abnormalities. ALS motor neurons exhibit hallmark metabolic defects including decreased mitochondrial respiration and increased glycolysis, which arise from systemic NAD+ depletion. SIRT3 activation and/or NAD+ supplementation has been discovered as a treatment for disease phenotypes in both sporadic and familial ALS, restoring normal mitochondrial metabolism and rescuing motor neuron viability.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 plays a crucial role in mitotic cell division regulation. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of proper cell cycle progression and mitotic fidelity. In addition to its roles in glutamine metabolism and tumor suppression, SIRT4 contributes to the orderly execution of mitosis, extending the functional repertoire of this mitochondrial sirtuin beyond metabolism.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT4
object: NSCLC, colorectal cancer, neuroblastoma, and gastric cancer
context: SIRT4 is an effective tumour suppressor in non-small cell lung cancer cells, human colorectal cancer, neuroblastoma, and gastric cancer. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of restrained tumour growth across multiple cancer types, in part by inhibiting glutamine metabolism and modulating mitochondrial dynamics. Low SIRT4 expression thereby permits tumorigenic behaviour, and SIRT4 represents a prognostic and therapeutic target in these cancers.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT4
object: hepatocellular carcinoma and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
context: Expression of SIRT4 is considerably downregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma tumour tissues and in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Lower expression of SIRT4 promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma development. Directionally, loss of SIRT4 sits upstream of tumorigenic progression in these cancers, and its reduced expression is associated with poorer outcomes, supporting SIRT4 as a biomarker and tumor suppressor in HCC and esophageal cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT4
object: endothelial cells of the umbilical vein and osteoarthritis
context: In humans, SIRT4 inhibits inflammation in endothelial cells of the umbilical vein and in osteoarthritis. SIRT4 suppresses the inflammatory response and oxidative stress in osteoarthritis. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of dampened inflammatory signalling in vascular endothelium and joint tissue. By restraining inflammation and oxidative stress, SIRT4 exerts protective effects in osteoarthritis and may help preserve endothelial function.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT4
context: As an outcome of cellular stresses, SIRT4 controls PTEN stability via the insulin-degrading enzyme (IDE). Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of PTEN protein abundance through IDE-mediated degradation. Because PTEN is a key tumour suppressor and negative regulator of PI3K/Akt signalling, SIRT4-dependent control of PTEN stability links mitochondrial sirtuin activity to oncogenic signalling under stress conditions.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 controls ATP homeostasis and uses AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) to mediate retrograde signalling. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of cellular energy sensing and mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication. By modulating ATP levels and engaging AMPK-mediated retrograde signalling, SIRT4 helps the cell adapt its nuclear gene expression to mitochondrial metabolic status under conditions of energy stress.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT5
context: In lung epithelial cells, SIRT5-mediated deacetylation of Forkhead protein FOXO3a inhibits apoptosis induced by cigarette smoke extract. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of FOXO3a deacetylation and reduced apoptosis under cigarette smoke stress. By dampening FOXO3a-driven pro-apoptotic signalling, SIRT5 helps lung epithelial cells survive the toxic effects of cigarette smoke, with potential relevance to smoking-related lung pathology.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT5
object: breast tumor, HCC, and NSCLC cells
context: SIRT5 is important in the growth of breast tumour cells, hepatocellular carcinoma, and human non-small cell lung cancer tissues. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of tumour growth in these cancer types, and its overexpression indicates a poor prognosis in human non-small cell lung cancer. SIRT5 thereby acts as a tumour-promoting factor in breast cancer, HCC, and lung cancer, making it a candidate therapeutic target.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 is upregulated during cellular transformation and is involved in cancer and its proliferation by desuccinylating serine hydroxymethyltransferase 2 (SHMT2). Directionally, SIRT5 desuccinylation of SHMT2 sits upstream of enhanced one-carbon metabolism and cancer cell proliferation. By activating SHMT2, SIRT5 supports the biosynthetic demands of proliferating cancer cells, contributing to tumorigenesis.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT5 desuccinylation of SDHA
object: clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumorigenesis
context: SIRT5-mediated desuccinylation of succinate dehydrogenase A (SDHA) promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumorigenesis. Directionally, SIRT5 desuccinylation of SDHA sits upstream of increased growth of clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumours. By activating SDHA and thereby modulating the TCA cycle, SIRT5 supports the metabolic reprogramming that drives this kidney cancer, identifying SIRT5 as a potential target in ccRCC.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT5
context: A finding suggests that in cardiomyocytes, SIRT5 is a key moderator in cell death induced by H2O2. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of the cardiomyocyte response to oxidative stress, dampening or modulating hydrogen peroxide-induced cell death. This places SIRT5 in the cardiac stress response network and suggests that modulating SIRT5 activity could influence oxidative injury in the heart.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT5
object: cellular energy metabolism and AMPK activity under energy stress
context: As a result of energy stress, SIRT5 modulates cellular energy metabolism and AMP-activated protein kinase activity. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of metabolic adaptation and AMPK activation during energy deprivation. By influencing energy metabolism and engaging AMPK signalling, SIRT5 helps cells maintain energy homeostasis under stress conditions, linking mitochondrial deacylation to the cellular energy sensing network.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT6
context: In humans, SIRT6 is necessary to maintain the telomere position effect. SIRT6 was discovered as the first enzyme that modifies histones to regulate the telomere position effect in human cells, a novel role for SIRT6 in the regulation of age-related genome silencing. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of telomeric chromatin silencing, providing a new approach for telomere chromatin silencing and linking SIRT6 to telomere biology and genome stability.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT6
object: aging and reprogramming of human iPSCs
context: SIRT6 has a part to play in ageing of human induced pluripotent stem cells as well as their reprogramming. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of pluripotent stem cell aging dynamics and the efficiency of somatic cell reprogramming. By influencing these processes, SIRT6 links chromatin-based ageing regulation to stem cell biology and regenerative medicine.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT6
context: Sirtuin 6 inhibits the generation of reactive oxygen species and glycolysis, which decreases the inflammatory response generated by hypoxia in human osteoblasts. This has therapeutic implications in inflammatory bone resorption. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of reduced ROS and glycolysis and thereby of dampened hypoxic inflammation in bone cells. SIRT6 thus protects osteoblasts from hypoxia-induced inflammatory damage.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT6 downregulation
context: Research has shown that senescence of endothelial cells is induced by oxidative stress due to SIRT6 downregulation. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of oxidative stress-driven endothelial senescence. Because SIRT6 normally supports antioxidant defences and DNA repair, its decline leaves endothelial cells vulnerable to oxidative damage and the senescent phenotype, linking SIRT6 to vascular ageing.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT6
context: It has been discovered in humans that SIRT6 interacts with the nuclear factor erythroid-derived 2-like 2 (NRF2) for the protection of mesenchymal stem cells from oxidative damage. SIRT6 safeguards human mesenchymal stem cells from oxidative stress by coactivating NRF2. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of NRF2-dependent antioxidant gene expression and thereby of stem cell survival under oxidative conditions.
