source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT6 overexpression
context: Compared to healthy cells, SIRT6 overexpression significantly accelerates apoptosis in tumour cells. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of tumour cell death, preferentially killing cancer cells while sparing healthy cells. This tumour-selective pro-apoptotic activity supports SIRT6 activation as a potential therapeutic strategy against cancers that retain SIRT6 expression.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT6 deficiency
context: Lack of SIRT6 decreases the viability of prostate cancer cells while increasing chemotherapeutic sensitivity. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of reduced prostate cancer cell survival and heightened responsiveness to chemotherapy. This indicates that targeting SIRT6 could render prostate cancer cells more vulnerable to cytotoxic agents, supporting SIRT6 inhibition as an adjunct to prostate cancer treatment.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT7
object: dependent on N- and C-terminal domains
context: The DNA-activated deacetylase activity of SIRT7 is dependent on both the N- and C-terminal domains. The SIRT7 N-terminal domain (NTD) is made up of three helices, and according to the findings SIRT7-NTD has structural similarities to transcription factor regulators and may have a role in DNA binding. Directionally, the SIRT7 NTD sits upstream of DNA binding and enzymatic activation, connecting SIRT7 structure to its chromatin-associated functions.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT7
object: aging and lifespan of hematopoietic cells
context: SIRT7 has deacetylase activity and plays a critical role in ageing and lifespan of hematopoietic cells in humans. SIRT7 is an influence factor in healthy aging and the development of age-dependent myeloid stem-cell disorders. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of haematopoietic stem cell maintenance and healthy aging, with dysregulation linked to age-dependent blood disorders.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 arginine methylation maintains energy balance by coordinating glucose availability with mitochondria biogenesis. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of the coupling between nutrient (glucose) status and mitochondrial mass. By linking glucose sensing to mitochondrial biogenesis, SIRT7 helps the cell match energy production to substrate availability, contributing to metabolic homeostasis.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT7
context: Sirtuin 7 is required not only for rDNA transcription but also for particular pre-rRNA cleavage. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of ribosomal RNA synthesis and processing in the nucleolus. By supporting both rDNA transcription and pre-rRNA cleavage, SIRT7 is essential for ribosome biogenesis, connecting SIRT7 to growth, protein synthesis, and cellular proliferation.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT7 depletion
context: SIRT7 depletion decreases DNA repair and compaction of chromatin, rendering cells more susceptible to genotoxic stressors. SIRT7 is a histone desuccinylase that functionally links to chromatin compaction and genome stability. Directionally, SIRT7 loss sits upstream of reduced genomic stability and increased sensitivity to DNA damage, making SIRT7 important for protecting cells against genotoxic stress.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT7
object: human stem cell aging as a heterochromatin stabilizer
context: SIRT7 antagonizes human stem cell aging as a heterochromatin stabiliser and safeguards chromatin structure. As a heterochromatin stabiliser, SIRT7 counteracts human stem cell ageing. SIRT7 also regulates innate immune modulation and ensures geroprotection during stem cell ageing. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of heterochromatin maintenance and stem cell rejuvenation, protecting stem cells from age-related chromatin deterioration.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT7 inactivation
context: SIRT7 inactivation reduces breast cancer metastasis by blocking TGF-β signalling. SIRT7 deacetylase activity inhibits metastasis of breast cancer by antagonising transforming growth factor-β signalling. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of TGF-β-driven metastasis in breast cancer. By promoting TGF-β signalling, SIRT7 supports the metastatic spread of breast cancer cells, and its inactivation curbs this process regardless of changes in original tumour development.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT7
object: colorectal, gastric, and luminal breast cancer
context: In humans, SIRT7 takes part in the genesis of colorectal cancer, gastric cancer, and luminal breast cancer. SIRT7 is overexpressed in multiple cancer tissues, promoting the survival of cancer cells and the maintenance of a transformed state. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of tumorigenesis in these cancer types, and its overexpression supports the transformed phenotype across a broad range of tumours.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: Butein, piceatannol and isoliquiritigenin
context: Plant polyphenols notably butein, piceatannol, and isoliquiritigenin (ILQ) have been demonstrated to activate recombinant SIRT1, and are known as sirtuin activating compounds (STACs). Directionally, these natural polyphenols sit upstream of enhanced SIRT1 enzymatic activity. Together with resveratrol, these plant-derived compounds represent natural STACs, and synthetic STACs such as SRT1720 activate SIRT1 substantially more potently.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol (3, 5, 4'-trihydroxystilbene) is a natural plant polyphenol found in grapes and red wines. In lower organisms, resveratrol replicates the effects of calorie restriction, and mice fed a high-fat diet have lower insulin resistance. STACs interact directly with SIRT1 and other isoforms, and resveratrol remains the most prominent natural sirtuin activator with longevity-relevant effects.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SRT1720
context: Many synthetic STACs that are chemically unrelated to resveratrol, such as those with an imidazo[1,2-b]thiazole core including SRT1720, activate SIRT1 substantially more potently than resveratrol. Directionally, SRT1720 sits upstream of enhanced SIRT1 activity, with higher potency than natural activators. These synthetic activators have been used in numerous studies to demonstrate their effect on SIRT1 and are being developed for therapeutic applications.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: Splitomicin
object: Sir2 in S. cerevisiae (weakly inhibits human SIRT1)
context: Splitomicin inhibits Sir2 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, but showed weaker inhibition on human SIRT1. Yeast Sir2 and human SIRT2 are inhibited by sirtinol. Directionally, these small-molecule sirtuin inhibitors (STICs) sit upstream of reduced sirtuin catalytic activity, with species- and isoform-selective potencies. Sirtuin inhibitors have also been considered for the treatment of Parkinson's disease, in addition to cancer therapy.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: Suramin
context: Suramin is a potent inhibitor of many sirtuins like SIRT1, SIRT2 and SIRT5. The majority of known sirtuin inhibitors exclusively inhibit SIRT1 and/or SIRT2, however some also inhibit SIRT3 and SIRT5 with reduced affinity. Cambinol has the most effective efficacy against Burkitt lymphoma cell lines, and Salermide causes apoptosis in cancer cells without relying on p53, with both inhibiting SIRT1 and SIRT2.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: Cambinol
context: Cambinol has the most effective efficacy against Burkitt lymphoma cell lines. Salermide causes apoptosis in cancer cells without relying on p53. Both Cambinol and Salermide have inhibitory effects on SIRT1 and SIRT2. Directionally, these sirtuin-inhibiting compounds sit upstream of suppressed cancer cell growth, with Cambinol showing particular potency against Burkitt lymphoma among the STIC class of sirtuin inhibitors.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT1 and SIRT2
context: SIRT1 and SIRT2 promote cell proliferation and play a pro-tumorigenic role in lung cancer. Expression of sirtuin 1 and 2 is associated with poor prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer patients. Directionally, SIRT1 and SIRT2 sit upstream of lung cancer cell proliferation and aggressive disease. Their elevated expression is linked to poor prognosis, supporting SIRT1 and SIRT2 as therapeutic targets and prognostic biomarkers in lung cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT3 deficiency
object: colon cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and migration
context: In colon cancer, SIRT3 deficiency reduces cell proliferation, invasion, and migration while increasing apoptosis. Directionally, SIRT3 loss sits upstream of restrained colon cancer aggressiveness and enhanced cell death. SIRT3 could also be used as a marker for colon cancer. These findings indicate that SIRT3 supports the aggressive behaviour of colon cancer cells, and its inhibition may represent an anti-tumour strategy.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT3 upregulation
object: glycolysis and proliferation in breast cancer cells
context: Upregulation of SIRT3 in breast cancer cells suppresses glycolysis and proliferation, offering a metabolic pathway for tumour suppression. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of reduced glycolytic metabolism and growth in breast cancer cells. By suppressing glycolysis, SIRT3 limits the Warburg-like metabolic program that supports breast cancer proliferation, identifying SIRT3 activation as a potential tumour-suppressive strategy in breast cancer.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 is found to be overexpressed in Parkinson's disease. SIRT2 is also overexpressed in neurodegenerative disorders generally and protects neural cells from oxidative damage caused by ageing and disease. Directionally, elevated SIRT2 sits upstream of neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease. Sirtuin inhibitors have been considered for the treatment of Parkinson's disease, alongside cancer therapy, because of this SIRT2 involvement.
source_document: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md

subject: Relocalization of Chromatin Modifiers (RCM) Hypothesis
object: aging results from progressive loss of epigenetic information
context: The Relocalization of Chromatin Modifiers (RCM) Hypothesis is a key framework in aging biology, primarily developed by David Sinclair and colleagues. It proposes that aging in eukaryotes results largely from the progressive loss of epigenetic information due to the repeated relocalization of chromatin-modifying proteins during DNA repair. Chromatin modifiers normally sit at specific genomic loci to maintain gene expression patterns that define cell identity, but are recruited to damage sites during repair, temporarily disrupting their original positions and altering local gene expression.
source_document: _document_ - relocalization of sirtuins - chromatin modifiers, grok.md

subject: Chromatin modifiers (SIRT1, SIRT6, HDAC1, PARP1)
context: Chromatin modifiers including sirtuins like SIRT1 and SIRT6, as well as HDAC1 and PARP1, normally sit at specific genomic loci to maintain proper gene expression patterns that define cell identity. When DNA damage, especially double-strand breaks, occurs, these proteins are recruited to damage sites to assist in repair. This temporarily disrupts their original positions, altering local gene expression, and repeated relocalization over a lifetime contributes to the progressive loss of epigenetic information.
source_document: _document_ - relocalization of sirtuins - chromatin modifiers, grok.md

subject: RCM (Relocalization of Chromatin Modifiers)
context: RCM likely evolved as a beneficial short-term response: relocalizing modifiers to damage sites helps cells survive acute threats by prioritizing repair and survival over normal gene regulation. In youth this is advantageous, but over a lifetime the cumulative failure to reset becomes detrimental, contributing to aging. This trade-off, where a trait that benefits early survival becomes harmful later in life, is the classic signature of antagonistic pleiotropy.
source_document: _document_ - relocalization of sirtuins - chromatin modifiers, grok.md

subject: Partial reprogramming
context: Partial reprogramming (e.g., via Yamanaka factors) can reset epigenetic information, supporting the idea that aging is reversible at the information level. This connection to cellular reprogramming complements the RCM hypothesis, which frames aging as an epigenetic software problem rather than purely hardware (mutation) damage. Because epigenetic changes can potentially be reset, unlike permanent mutations, reprogramming-based approaches offer a route to restoring youthful gene expression patterns.
source_document: _document_ - relocalization of sirtuins - chromatin modifiers, grok.md

subject: DSB repair and RCM
context: DSB repair and RCM may advance epigenetic clocks by affecting DNA methylation machinery (e.g., TET enzymes and DNMTs). Because the response to DNA damage follows conserved mechanisms, aging becomes somewhat predictable despite random damage, leading to consistent epigenetic drift. Directionally, DNA damage repair and the consequent relocalization of chromatin modifiers sit upstream of clock-measured epigenetic age acceleration, linking RCM to quantitative measures of biological aging.
source_document: _document_ - relocalization of sirtuins - chromatin modifiers, grok.md

subject: SIRT6 loss
object: severe metabolic defects and rapid aging
context: Zhao et al. note that loss of SIRT6 causes severe metabolic defects and rapid aging, positioning SIRT6 as holding the most potential for actual mammalian life-span extension.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7 depletion
context: Global SIRT7 depletion contributes to premature ageing, especially in the backbone, white adipose tissue, and the heart.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: Resveratrol
context: Resveratrol, a red-wine polyphenol, is a prototypical sirtuin-activating compound (STAC) that allosterically activates SIRT1 (lowering Km for substrate and NAD+) and extends lifespan in yeast, worms, flies, and mice on a high-calorie diet (Howitz et al., 2003, Nature 425:191-196, PMID 12805428; Baur et al., 2006, Nature 444:337-342, PMID 17086191).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: Resveratrol
object: leukemia, DMBA-induced mammary tumors, skin cancer, prostate cancer
context: Resveratrol exhibits chemopreventive activity against leukemia, DMBA-induced mammary tumors, skin cancer, and other malignancies, in part through SIRT1-dependent and -independent pathways (reviewed in the sirtuin literature; Baur 2006 PMID 17086191).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: STACs
context: Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) such as resveratrol engage a 'K-type' allosteric mechanism that lowers the Michaelis constant (Km) of SIRT1 for both the acetylated substrate and NAD+, increasing catalytic efficiency (Howitz 2003 PMID 12805428; structurally characterized in SIRT1-resveratrol complexes, PMID 26109052).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: NAD-boosting molecules (NMN, NR)
context: NAD+-boosting molecules (NMN, NR) raise cellular NAD+, relieving nicotinamide feedback inhibition and activating all seven sirtuins (SIRT1-SIRT7).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: CD38 inhibitors (apigenin, quercetin)
context: CD38 consumes NAD+; inhibiting it (apigenin, quercetin) boosts NAD+ availability, the obligate co-substrate for all sirtuins (and thus for SIRT1-SIRT7 activity).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1 brain-specific knockout
context: Brain-specific SIRT1 knockout elevates β-amyloid plaques and gliosis, implicating SIRT1 in Alzheimer's protection (per the review's neurobiology section).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 conferred neuroprotection in three different mouse models of Huntington's disease; overexpression attenuated mutant huntingtin neurotoxicity.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1 overexpression
context: SIRT1 overexpression reduces α-synuclein aggregates, supporting a role in Parkinson's protection (via FOXO/autophagy pathways).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: Endothelial SIRT1 depletion
context: Endothelial SIRT1 depletion is associated with cardiovascular diseases, reflecting SIRT1's vascular protective (eNOS/NO, anti-inflammatory) roles.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 counteracts atherosclerosis by inhibiting VSMC hypertrophy and NF-κB-driven inflammation.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 prevents cardiac hypertrophy during ageing; its deacetylase activity protects against age-related cardiac hypertrophy.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6 expression
context: SIRT6 expression blocks the development of cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7 deletion
context: SIRT7 deletion leads to heart hypertrophy, fibrosis, lipofuscin accumulation, and inflammatory cardiomyopathy that worsens with age.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1 overexpression
context: SIRT1 overexpression protects against obesity-associated metabolic derangement via deacetylation of metabolic transcription factors.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1 and SIRT1 activators
context: SIRT1 and its activators prevent/reverse insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes by enhancing deacetylation of metabolic regulators (e.g., PGC-1α, FOXO; Rodgers 2005 PMID 15931387).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 activates PEPCK (gluconeogenesis) via deacetylation (e.g., FOXO, c-Myc, G6PD, PEPCK), influencing transcription, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, and redox balance.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 activates GDH to support gluconeogenesis from amino acids via deacetylation.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 indirectly destabilizes HIF1α and subsequently inhibits glycolysis and glucose oxidation.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6 overexpression
context: SIRT6 overexpression protects mice from diet-induced obesity, with increased glucose tolerance and reduced fat accumulation.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7 knockout
context: SIRT7 knockout mice are resistant to glucose intolerance and show improved insulin sensitivity on a high-fat diet.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 has a dual role in cancer (tumor suppressor and promoter): it can act as tumor suppressor (via p53/β-catenin/survivin restraint) or tumor promoter (via p53 deacetylation), depending on context.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 is described as tumor suppressor protein (TSP); it is a tumor-suppressor protein whose deficiency causes genomic instability and premature aging.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 is described as oncogene (upregulated in cancers); it is upregulated in cancers and acts as an oncogene in several contexts (Barber 2012 PMID 22722849).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 is described as tumor suppressor (downregulated in cancers); it is a tumor suppressor downregulated in multiple cancers (Wu et al., 2022).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 is described as tumor suppressor (decreased in breast/ovarian cancers); it is a tumor suppressor frequently downregulated in breast/ovarian cancers (Massudi et al., 2012).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 is a central mediator of healthspan and longevity: its activity declines with age as NAD+ falls, and genetic/pharmacologic (resveratrol, NAD+ precursors) activation extends lifespan in model organisms; SIRT1-dependent deacetylation of p53, FOXOs, and NF-κB underpins these effects (Giblin et al., 2014, Sirtuins: Guardians of Mammalian Healthspan; Satoh et al., 2013 brain-specific SIRT1-overexpression lifespan extension, PMID 24011076).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 relocalizes to DNA double-strand breaks, where it deacetylates H4K16 and other targets to promote homologous-recombination repair and maintain heterochromatin, supporting genomic stability with age; its decline with falling NAD+ impairs this DDR coupling (Oberdoerffer et al., 2008, PMC2853975).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 governs cell-cycle checkpoints by deacetylating p53 (reducing its transcriptional activity) and RB, supporting DNA-repair-coupled arrest rather than apoptosis or premature senescence; age-related SIRT1 decline biases G1/S and G2/M responses toward senescence (reviewed in the source review).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: SIRT1 opposes cellular senescence by deacetylating p53, FOXOs, p66Shc, and histones at SASP loci: SIRT1 activation reduces SASP factor secretion (including IL-6 and PAI-1) and delays replicative/oncogene-induced senescence, while its decline with age is a driver of the senescence phenotype (source review; Giblin et al., 2014).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: eNOS-derived nitric oxide activates SIRT1, and SIRT1 deacetylates eNOS to maintain its activity, forming a reciprocal endothelial-protective loop that declines with age; this NO/SIRT1 axis supports cardiovascular healthspan (Mattagajasingh et al., 2007; listed as a positive regulator in the source review's Table 3).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: Estrogen receptor β (Erβ) signaling upregulates SIRT1 expression and activity, linking estrogens to SIRT1-mediated metabolic and neuroprotective programs; estrogen-replacement models show increased SIRT1 levels and reduced oxidative damage (source review Table 3 lists Erβ as a positive SIRT1 regulator).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: FOXO3 and SIRT1 form a feed-forward stress-resistance loop: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3 to shunt it toward stress-resistance and metabolic genes, while FOXO3 transactivates SIRT1 expression; this mutually reinforcing pair is central to longevity-associated signalling (Brunet et al., 2004, PMID 15066266).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: PAI-1, a senescence-associated secreted factor (SASP), suppresses SIRT1 expression, and SIRT1 reciprocally binds the PAI-1 promoter to deacetylate H4K16 and repress its transcription; elevation of PAI-1 with age thus contributes to SIRT1 decline and the senescence phenotype (Kortlever et al., 2006, Nat Cell Biol; Wan et al., 2014, Aging Cell, PMID 24649892).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: p53 directly represses SIRT1 transcription by binding the SIRT1 promoter; conversely SIRT1 deacetylates p53, creating a p53-SIRT1 regulatory loop in which DNA damage and p53 activation lower SIRT1 and bias cells toward apoptosis/senescence (Nemoto et al., 2004).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: p16INK4a (CDKN2A) accumulation with age drives senescence and opposes SIRT1-dependent replicative programs; SIRT1 represses p16INK4a expression via promoter deacetylation and via the Akt/p70S6K1 axis, and p16INK4a upregulation is a hallmark of aging-related SIRT1 decline (Li & Tollefsbol, 2011, PLoS One 6:e17421, PMID 21390332).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: NF-κB signaling suppresses SIRT1 (e.g., via promoter occupancy and microRNAs) while SIRT1 deacetylates p65/RelA on Lys310 to dampen NF-κB transcription, creating a pro-inflammatory, pro-senescence feedback as SIRT1 declines with age (source review Table 3; aging-associated NF-κB activation opposes SIRT1 programs).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: p66Shc, a lifespan-associated redox adapter, is repressed by SIRT1 (SIRT1 knockdown raises p66Shc), and p66Shc elevation promotes reactive-oxygen species generation and endothelial dysfunction, contributing to SIRT1 decline and vascular aging (Zhou et al., 2011, PMID 21778425).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: LKB1, through AMPK activation, feeds back on SIRT1 via NAD+-dependent coupling (AMPK raises NAD+), but is also listed as a negative pathway regulator in Table 3: under certain conditions AMPK/LKB1 signaling opposes SIRT1-promoted anabolic programs, reflecting context-dependent cross-talk of the energy-sensing network.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: Cyclin D1/CDK4 and the cyclin B-Cdk1 complex regulate SIRT1 by phosphorylation (massive phosphorylation is required for SIRT1 cell-cycle function), and cyclin D1 opposes SIRT1-dependent regulation of cell-cycle genes in proliferative contexts; Table 3 lists Cyclin D1 among negative SIRT1 regulators (Sasaki et al., 2008, PLoS One 3:e4020, PMID 19015735).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT1
context: mTORC1/S6K1 signaling opposes SIRT1-promoted catabolic and stress-resistance programs (while SIRT1/SIRT2 deacetylate S6K1 to license its activity, making regulation bidirectional and nutrient-dependent); rapamycin-mediated mTOR inhibition raises NAD+ and benefits from SIRT1 coupling, as reflected in Table 3's classification of the mTOR/S6K pathway as a SIRT1 negative regulator.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 is a cytoplasmic/mitotic deacetylase that regulates cytokinesis and the G2/M transition, supporting genomic stability and mitotic fidelity; age-related SIRT2 decline impairs these cell-cycle checkpoints (source review; North & Verdin review of SIRT2 mitotic roles).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: BubR1, a spindle-assembly-checkpoint protein, is stabilized by SIRT2 deacetylation at Lys668 (SIRT2 knockdown accelerates BubR1 degradation); SIRT2 overexpression increases BubR1 levels and delays aging phenotypes in progeroid mice, so BubR1 is functionally a positive downstream effector of the SIRT2 pathway (North et al., 2014, Cell, PMID 24825348).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 deacetylates G6PD in the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) at Lys403, activating it to promote NADPH production and antioxidant defense; the PPP thus serves as a downstream effector of SIRT2 and is listed among its positive pathway regulators (Wang et al., 2014, Cell Metab, PMID 24769394).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: As a class III NAD+-dependent deacetylase, SIRT2 activity is directly governed by NAD+ availability; NAD+ precursors (e.g., NMN, NR) boost SIRT2 activity in mitosis and metabolism, linking NAD+ decline in aging to reduced SIRT2 function (source review).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 deacetylates FOXO1 and FOXO3a, promoting their nuclear accumulation and target-gene activation (e.g., stress resistance, gluconeogenesis, and cell survival) in a manner analogous to SIRT1-FOXO coupling, making FOXOs downstream effectors and listed positive regulators of the SIRT2 pathway (Wang et al., 2007, PMID 17521387).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: SIRT2 promotes antioxidant defense in part through induction/stabilization of MnSOD (SOD2) targets, reducing mitochondrial superoxide; MnSOD is therefore listed among the positive regulators/effectors of the SIRT2 pathway in the source review's Table 3.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: β-catenin (Wnt pathway) transcriptionally represses the SIRT2 promoter, and SIRT2 reciprocally deacetylates β-catenin to destabilize it, so Wnt signaling opposes SIRT2 pathway activity and vice versa in intestinal and cancer cell contexts (BBA Mol Cell Res 2021).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: Akt signaling is associated with inhibition of SIRT2-dependent cell-cycle and stress outputs (e.g., cyclin E-CDK2 phosphorylates SIRT2 at Ser331 to reduce its deacetylase activity), placing AKT signaling among negative regulators of the SIRT2 pathway (Pandithage et al., 2008, J Cell Biol, PMID 18504304).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT2
context: NF-κB activation opposes SIRT2-dependent anti-inflammatory and cell-cycle programs, while SIRT2 deacetylates p65 to dampen NF-κB responses; Table 3 lists NF-κB among negative regulators of the SIRT2 pathway in aging.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 is the principal mitochondrial deacetylase, regulating the majority of the mitochondrial acetylome to sustain oxidative-phosphorylation enzymes, fatty-acid oxidation, and the TCA/mitochondrial electron transport chain; SIRT3 declines with age, impairing mitochondrial function (source review; Hebert et al., 2013).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 deacetylates and activates SOD2 (MnSOD) at Lys68/Lys122 and supports glutathione-dependent antioxidant pathways, reducing mitochondrial ROS; aging-associated SIRT3 decline increases oxidative stress, and SIRT3 knockout mice show accelerated aging phenotypes (source review; Qiu et al., 2010).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: SIRT3 G477T and other SNPs are associated with human longevity/healthy aging; the G477T variant (V208I/V184I alleles) improves SIRT3 function or expression and is enriched in centenarian populations in some cohorts (source review; Rose et al., 2003, Alì et al., 2015 reports).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: FOXO3a translocates to mitochondria where it binds the SIRT3 promoter and induces SIRT3 expression, which in turn activates MnSOD to reduce ROS, forming a FOXO3a-SIRT3-PGC-1α mitochondrial-protective loop (source review; Tseng et al., 2013; also PMC2532794).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: MnSOD (SOD2) functions as a key downstream effector of SIRT3: SIRT3 deacetylates MnSOD to activate it, and the two cooperate in neutralizing mitochondrial ROS; MnSOD is thus listed among positive regulators/effectors of the SIRT3 pathway in Table 3.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: NF-κB (p65 at Ser536) occupies the SIRT3 promoter and represses SIRT3 transcription, so pro-inflammatory NF-κB activation lowers SIRT3 and mitochondrial antioxidant capacity; Table 3 lists NF-κB among negative regulators of the SIRT3 pathway (Wang et al., 2021 preprint evidence).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: MAPK/ERK signaling can oppose SIRT3-dependent metabolic and antioxidant outputs (e.g., ERK-driven proliferative/fibrotic signaling coupling with SIRT3 decrease); Table 3 lists MAPK/ERK among negative regulators of the SIRT3 pathway in aging.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT3
context: PI3K/AKT signaling regulates Sirt3 in various contexts, generally opposing SIRT3-mediated catabolic/mitochondrial programs (e.g., PI3K/AKT modulates Sirt3 in activated microglia); Table 3 lists PI3K/AKT among negative regulators of the SIRT3 pathway (PMID 37930585).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 inhibits fatty-acid oxidation at the mitochondria by suppressing malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MCD) ADP-ribosylase activity and restraining oxidative fuel use, an adaptive suppression that rises under calorie restriction; during aging its dysregulation perturbs metabolic fuel selection (source review).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4
context: SIRT4 suppresses apoptosis mainly by inhibiting mitochondrial glutamine metabolism (ADP-ribosylating GDH) and by dampening inducers such as PGC-1α/AMPK, protecting cells from genotoxic stress; SIRT4 loss in contexts like HCC promotes apoptosis, while its decline with stress affects tumor suppression and aging (source review).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4
context: NF-κB signaling suppresses SIRT4 in tumor and inflammatory contexts, consistent with the pro-inflammatory axis opposing SIRT4's tumor-suppressive and metabolic-restraining functions; Table 3 lists NF-κB among negative regulators of the SIRT4 pathway.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4
context: Pro-apoptotic Bax opposes SIRT4's anti-apoptotic effects on mitochondria; under stress Bax-mediated mitochondrial permeabilization is associated with decreased SIRT4-mediated protection, so Bax is listed among negative regulators of SIRT4 in Table 3.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4
context: Caspase activation, hallmark of the intrinsic apoptosis pathway, is antagonistic to SIRT4's mitochondrial anti-apoptotic function; during apoptosis caspases cleave/deregulate mitochondrial effectors, placing caspases among negative regulators of the SIRT4 pathway (Table 3).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4
context: GDH is the primary substrate through which SIRT4 suppresses glutamine metabolism, yet GDH is also listed among negative regulators in Table 3: high GDH activity can outpace SIRT4 ADP-ribosylation under energetic stress, switching cells toward glutaminolysis/fuel oxidation and away from SIRT4-mediated restraint.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT4
context: AMPK activation (energy stress) opposes SIRT4's anabolic bias by promoting catabolism and mitochondrial biogenesis; reciprocal to SIRT4's inhibition of AMPK, AMPK signaling is thus classified among negative regulators of the SIRT4 pathway in Table 3.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 regulates fuel oxidation via desuccinylation/deglycylidation of mitochondrial enzymes including CPS1 and components of fatty-acid oxidation, supporting metabolic flexibility under fasting and during aging; its age-related changes affect liver and muscle energetics (source review; Park et al., 2013).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 desuccinylates enzymes of the urea cycle and electron-transport chain to sustain mitochondrial function under ammonia and oxidative stress, mitigating accumulation of damaged mitochondria with age; it also supports antioxidant capacity during fasting (source review; Nakagawa et al., 2009).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5
context: Anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 inhibits apoptosis, thereby opposing SIRT5's pro-survival species; in Table 3 Bcl-2 is listed among negative regulators of the SIRT5 pathway in contexts where SIRT5's effects depend on cell survival/Apoptosis signaling.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 desuccinylates GDH to inhibit its activity (opposite to SIRT4, which ADP-ribosylates GDH), so high GDH activity counters SIRT5-dependent restraint of glutamine metabolism; GDH is listed among negative regulators of the SIRT5 pathway in Table 3.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT5
context: SIRT5 desuccinylates pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) to suppress its activity, favoring glutamine-dependent anaplerosis over glucose oxidation; PDH activity is thus reciprocally regulated and listed among negative regulators/opponents of SIRT5's metabolic program in Table 3 (Park et al., 2013, PMC3769971).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 overexpression extends lifespan in male mice and is required for healthy aging, acting through DNA repair, metabolic regulation, and inflammation control; as with SIRT1, SIRT6 activity is NAD+-dependent and declines with age (Kanfi et al., 2012, Nature; source review).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 is a core DNA double-strand-break repair factor: it is recruited to DSBs, deacetylates H3K9/H3K56 and CtIP, and stimulates PARP1 to promote homologous recombination and maintenance of genomic stability (Kaidi et al., 2010, PMC2943420).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 on telomeric chromatin and suppresses LINE-1 retrotransposon activity, maintaining genome stability and telomere function; SIRT6-deficient cells show genomic instability, telomere defects, and cellular senescence (Michishita et al., 2008; Van Meter et al., 2014).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 at telomeres and stabilizes WRN helicase, preventing telomere dysfunction-induced senescence; SIRT6-depleted cells undergo accelerated telomere replication problems and senescence (Michishita et al., 2008, Cell; source review).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: Nrf2, the master antioxidant transcription factor, induces SIRT6-responsive antioxidant and DNA-repair programs; SIRT6 binds the Nrf2 promoter and cooperates with Nrf2 to maintain glutathione and redox balance, and Nrf2 deacetylation is itself regulated by SIRT6 (Pan et al., 2016, Cell Res).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: In the vasculature, eNOS/NO signaling and SIRT6 cooperate in endothelial protection and vasodilation (analogous to the SIRT1-eNOS loop), so eNOS is listed as a positive regulator of the SIRT6 pathway in Table 3.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: IGF-1/AKT signaling can modulate SIRT6 activity and expression in metabolic and intestinal-fitness contexts, generally promoting SIRT6-dependent metabolic and tumor-suppressive programs; Table 3 lists IGF-1/AKT among positive regulators of the SIRT6 pathway.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 cooperates with p53 in DNA-damage responses (maintaining p53 activity under oxidative stress and supporting p21-dependent checkpoints), and p53 is listed among positive regulators of the SIRT6 pathway in Table 3 for DDR contexts.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: p21 (CDKN1A), whose expression is antagonized by SIRT6 (SIRT6 suppresses p21-driven senescence), accumulates with age and opposes SIRT6-regulated cell-cycle and DNA-repair programs; Table 3 lists p21 among negative regulators of SIRT6 (source review).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 on NF-κB (p65) target-gene promoters to repress NF-κB-dependent inflammation, and conversely NF-κB activation opposes SIRT6's anti-inflammatory/genome-stability program in aging; Table 3 lists NF-κB among negative regulators of SIRT6 (Kawahara et al., 2009, Cell).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: ICAM-1, an endothelial/leukocyte adhesion molecule elevated during inflammation and aging, is a target of SIRT6-repressed NF-κB signaling; its upregulation opposes SIRT6's vascular-protective role and it is listed among negative regulators of the SIRT6 pathway in Table 3.
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT6
context: PAI-1 is transcriptionally repressed by SIRT6 through H3K9 deacetylation at its promoter (SIRT6 binding is a hallmark of PAI-1 downregulation), so PAI-1 elevation with age opposes SIRT6's anti-senescence and metabolic programs; Table 3 lists PAI-1 among negative regulators of SIRT6 (Van Meter et al., 2014).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 deacetylates H3K18 on promoters (Barber et al., 2012, Nature, PMID 22722849) and associates with chromatin remodelers (including PAF1 complex) to regulate rDNA transcription, ribosomal biogenesis, and global gene expression; age-related SIRT7 decline perturbs these epigenetic landscapes (source review; Vakhrusheva et al., 2008).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 promotes cellular stress resistance by suppressing ER stress and reactive-ROS programs via Myc-linked silencing of ribosomal protein genes and by stabilizing DNA repair; SIRT7-depleted cells show increased apoptosis and metabolic stress (Shin et al., 2013, PMID 24210820; source review).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 is required for RNA polymerase I transcription and cell survival: its knockdown reduces Pol I association with rDNA and triggers apoptosis, and it deacetylates p53 in HCC cells to dampen p53-driven apoptosis, linking SIRT7 decline to age-related apoptosis and disease (Ford et al., 2006, Genes Dev 20:1075; source review).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7
context: FOXO3 is a positive regulator of the SIRT7 pathway: FOXO factors interact with SIRT7 to promote stress resistance, while SIRT7 deacetylates FOXO3 to prevent pro-apoptotic Ser574 phosphorylation, forming a mutual-activation loop (source review Table 3; SIRT7-FOXO3 cooperation).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7
context: The SIRT7-Myc axis is bidirectional: SIRT7 assembles with Myc at ribosomal protein (RP) gene promoters to silence gene expression and relieve ER stress, while Myc-driven proliferation opposes SIRT7-dependent growth-quiescence programs in some contexts; Table 3 lists Myc among negative regulators of SIRT7 (Shin et al., 2013, PMID 24210820).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 suppresses HIF-1α/2α protein levels (deacetylation-coupled destabilization), reducing hypoxic gene activation, and reciprocally HIF-1α is listed as a negative regulator of the SIRT7 pathway, an opposition relevant to tumor metabolism and aging (Hubbi et al., 2013, PMC3774348).
source_document: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md

subject: SIRT7
context: SIRT7 deacetylates p53 to repress p53-driven apoptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma, and p53 activation reciprocally opposes SIRT7 functions (e.g., under genotoxic stress p53 promotes apoptosis despite SIRT7), so p53 is listed among negative regulators of the SIRT7 pathway (source review; oncogene review s41388-024-02976-8).
